title: Password reset
prompt: A teammate wrote this spec. Find the situations it does not answer, where two engineers could build two different things. One per line.
spec: When a user forgets their password, they enter their email and we send them a reset link. Clicking the link lets them choose a new password. The link expires after a while.

hiddenCases.title: How long is 'a while'?
hiddenCases.description: The expiry time is not defined (15 minutes? 24 hours?).

hiddenCases.title: Email not registered
hiddenCases.description: What happens when the email is not registered? Do we say so (leaks which emails exist) or show the same message?

hiddenCases.title: Several reset requests
hiddenCases.description: If the user asks twice, do older links still work, or does a new link cancel the old ones?

hiddenCases.title: Link used twice
hiddenCases.description: Can a link be used more than once after the password is changed?

hiddenCases.title: Other sessions
hiddenCases.description: After the reset, are other logged-in sessions/devices signed out?

hiddenCases.title: Spam / abuse
hiddenCases.description: Is there a limit on how many reset emails can be requested (spam, abuse)?

hiddenCases.title: New password rules
hiddenCases.description: What rules apply to the new password? Can it equal the old one?

hiddenCases.title: Lost email access
hiddenCases.description: What if the user no longer has access to that email address?

hints: Read every vague word and ask 'how much, exactly?'
Think like an attacker. Think like a user who clicks everything twice.

title: Refund policy
prompt: Support agents will apply this policy word for word. Where will two agents decide differently? One case per line.
spec: Customers can get a full refund within 30 days of purchase if they are not satisfied. Items must be returned in their original condition.

hiddenCases.title: Which 30 days?
hiddenCases.description: Does day 1 start at purchase, shipping, or delivery? Calendar or business days? Which time zone ends day 30?

hiddenCases.title: What is 'original condition'?
hiddenCases.description: Opened box? Tried on? Missing tags or packaging?

hiddenCases.title: What is 'full'?
hiddenCases.description: Does 'full refund' include shipping fees and return shipping? Who pays return postage?

hiddenCases.title: Who judges 'not satisfied'?
hiddenCases.description: Must the customer give a reason? Can an agent refuse because the reason is weak?

hiddenCases.title: Discounts, gifts, bundles
hiddenCases.description: Refund amount for discounted items, gift purchases, coupons, or items in a bundle.

hiddenCases.title: Refund to where?
hiddenCases.description: Refund to the original payment method, store credit, or cash? What if that card is closed?

hiddenCases.title: Partial returns
hiddenCases.description: Can a customer return part of an order, or a damaged/faulty item outside 30 days?

hints: Every noun in the spec hides a question: which purchase? which day? which condition?
Think about money: shipping, coupons, gift cards.

title: Meeting scheduler
prompt: This is the whole spec for a 'find a time' feature. Find the cases it does not cover. One per line.
spec: The scheduler looks at everyone's calendar and books the first free one-hour slot next week during working hours.

hiddenCases.title: Time zones
hiddenCases.description: Whose working hours, when attendees are in different time zones?

hiddenCases.title: No free slot
hiddenCases.description: What if there is no common free hour next week?

hiddenCases.title: Tentative / private events
hiddenCases.description: How to treat tentative, private, or 'free' marked events, and all-day events?

hiddenCases.title: Optional attendees
hiddenCases.description: Must everyone be free, or only required attendees? What about rooms?

hiddenCases.title: Which is 'first'?
hiddenCases.description: First by time from Monday 00:00 in whose zone? Prefer mornings? Does it skip lunch?

hiddenCases.title: Race / double booking
hiddenCases.description: Someone's calendar changes between checking and booking; two schedulers grab the same slot.

hiddenCases.title: What is 'next week'?
hiddenCases.description: Calendar week vs next 7 days; asked on a Sunday; public holidays.

hiddenCases.title: Calendar access
hiddenCases.description: What if the scheduler cannot read someone's calendar (permissions, external guests)?

hints: Think about a team in London and San Francisco.
Think about what happens when the answer is 'nothing'.

title: Bank transfer invariant
prompt: Write the rule that must ALWAYS be true about a money transfer between two accounts in the same bank, no matter when it fails. One or two sentences, with "must".
intent: Money is conserved: at every moment (including if the transfer fails midway), the sum of the two balances equals the sum before the transfer; the debit and the credit happen together or not at all (atomic). Optionally: the sender's balance must never go below zero (or below the overdraft limit).
hints: Imagine the server crashes right after taking the money out of account A.
exampleGood: At every moment, the sum of the two account balances must equal the sum before the transfer started. The debit from A and the credit to B must both happen or neither happens.

title: Elevator door safety
prompt: Write the safety rule for an elevator that must hold in every state. One sentence with "must" or "must not".
intent: The elevator car must never move unless its doors are fully closed (equivalently: the doors must never be open while the car is moving, and the doors must only open when the car is stopped at a floor).
hints: Which two things must never be true at the same time?
"The elevator" could mean the car or the whole system. Be exact.
exampleGood: The elevator car must not move unless all of its doors are fully closed and locked.

title: Login lockout rule
prompt: Write a precise lockout rule: after too many wrong passwords, the account locks. Make every number and every 'reset' explicit. Two sentences max.
intent: After N (a number) consecutive failed login attempts for one account within a fixed window, the account is locked for a fixed duration (or until an admin unlocks it); a successful login resets the failure counter. Numbers must be explicit; 'consecutive' or the time window must be defined.
hints: Does the count reset after a success? After time?
exampleGood: After 5 consecutive failed login attempts on one account, the system must lock that account for 15 minutes. A successful login must reset the failed-attempt count to 0.
